title: ALMA constraints on the faint millimetre source number counts and their contribution to the cosmic infrared background
question: What are the faint (sub-mJy) number counts of millimetre sources at 1.1 and 1.3 mm from deep ALMA maps, and what fraction of the cosmic infrared background do they resolve?

data.sensitivity: 7.8 to 52.1 μJy/beam rms in 18 continuum maps

what.value: Bright-end 1.1 mm number counts (two faintest bins excluded)

evidence.quote: However, the two faintest bins in the latter data are not considered when comparing models or when fitting analytic functions
We adopted a spectral index $\beta = 2.0$ and dust temperature T = 35 K from (cite: Greve:2012)

what.value: CIB from COBE: 25 (+22/-13) Jy/deg2 at 1.1 mm and 17 (+16/-9) at 1.3 mm
Faint 1.3 mm counts from ALMA for comparison

evidence.quote: At 1.3 mm, the differential number counts of (cite: Hatsukade:2013) (orange symbols), which are obtained from sources with S/N$\geq4$, are consistent with our results within the uncertainties

recipe.method: CASA reduction, data weights rescaled for some fields, continuum imaged from line-free channels with natural weighting
key_parameters: natural weighting; extraction within two primary beams (~20 arcsec diameter)

recipe.goal: Extract sources and set the detection threshold
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fit candidates with S/N>3.5 and size consistent with beam (at most 1.5x beam); negative-map test and blank-field simulations used to assess spurious sources
Inject artificial sources, 1000 iterations per map, 4-8 per simulation, in 0.05-1 mJy; recovered if S/N>=3.5; A_survey = sum C_i A_i
Inject sources with S/N 3-8 in maps not corrected for primary beam, 10^4 repeats, boost = S_out/S_in vs S/N
Modified blackbody scaling; sources with lambda<1.2 mm scaled to 1.1 mm, others to 1.3 mm
key_parameters: beta = 2.0, T = 35 K, z=2; errors tested over 1<z<6, 20<T<60 K, 1.5<beta<2
assumptions: SMG-like SED for all faint sources

recipe.method: Sum of (1-f_c)/A_survey in bins of dLogS=0.2, scaled to 1; f_c = negative/positive ratio at source S/N; errors from Poisson (Gehrels), cosmic variance (Moster tool), completeness/boosting
software: Moster et al. 2011 cosmic variance tool
key_parameters: cosmic variance with z=3.5, dz=3, M*=10^10.5 Msun

recipe.method: chi2 minimisation of three-parameter Schechter function, separately at 1.1 and 1.3 mm, using this work plus literature counts

recipe.goal: Integrate counts and compare with CIB
recipe.method: Integrate dN/dS * S above S_lim; compare to COBE CIB of Fixsen 1998; convert 60 μJy at 1.3 mm to L_IR and SFR
assumptions: 1.3 mm flux corresponds to redshift-independent IR luminosity for 0.5<z<15; SFR from Kennicutt & Evans 2012

evidence.quote: In the 18 continuum maps, we detected 50 sources with S/N in the range 3.5-38.4

${\rm \sim9.5\times10^{-4} 
 \ deg^2}$ at 1.1 mm and ${\rm \sim6.6\times10^{-4} \  deg^2}$ at 1.3 mm
At S/N = 3.5, the boost fraction is $\simeq$1.09

answer_key.quantity: Integrated flux density resolved at 1.1 mm (S>0.1 mJy)
Integrated flux density resolved at 1.3 mm (S>0.06 mJy)

evidence.quote:
corresponds to a total IR luminosity $\rm L(8-1000\mu m)=6~\times10^{44}~erg~s^{-1}$, corresponding to a $\rm
